name: cachefiles_cull
prose: Precondition: cache, dir and filename are valid; dir is a directory dentry of the cache and the caller does NOT hold dir's inode lock (cachefiles_lookup_for_cull takes it itself). Postcondition: if the lookup fails (including -ENOENT for a missing or negative entry, -EBUSY if the victim already has S_KERNEL_FILE set, or any lookup_one error) the function returns that PTR_ERR value unchanged, with dir's inode lock already released by the lookup and no reference held. Otherwise, under the victim's inode lock, if S_KERNEL_FILE is now set the internal result is -EBUSY, else S_KERNEL_FILE is set on the victim; on -EBUSY dir's inode lock is released here, the victim dentry reference is dropped, and the error label converts it to -EIO (pr_err is logged), so this race returns -EIO and not -EBUSY. Otherwise cachefiles_bury_object is called (it releases dir's inode lock on all paths): on success fscache_count_culled is called, the victim reference is dropped and 0 is returned; on failure the victim reference is dropped, -ENOENT becomes -ESTALE, -ENOMEM is returned as -ENOMEM, and any other error is logged and returned as -EIO (S_KERNEL_FILE stays set on the victim in the burying-failure case). On every return dir's inode lock is released and the victim reference is dropped.
note: Prose rewritten: lookup_for_cull takes dir's lock (caller does not hold it); in-use race returns -EIO; -EBUSY from the early lookup passes through unchanged.

name: ceph_set_acl
prose: Precondition: dentry is a valid dentry with a valid inode; acl is NULL (remove the ACL) or a valid posix_acl owned by the caller; type is an ACL type. Postcondition: returns -EROFS if the inode is a snapshot inode (ceph_snap != CEPH_NOSNAP) with nothing changed; for type ACL_TYPE_ACCESS with non-NULL acl, posix_acl_update_mode may fail and its error is returned (it may also drop acl to NULL if the ACL is representable by the mode, in which case the xattr is removed); for ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT on a non-directory it returns -EINVAL if acl is non-NULL and 0 if acl is NULL, modifying nothing and caching nothing; for any other type it returns -EINVAL. With a non-NULL acl a buffer is kmalloc'd (-ENOMEM on failure) and the ACL is encoded (a negative return of posix_acl_to_xattr is returned); if the mode changed, __ceph_setattr is called to set mode/ctime and its nonzero error is returned; then __ceph_setxattr sets (or removes, when value is NULL) the ACL xattr: on its failure the old mode and ctime are restored via __ceph_setattr if the mode had been changed, and its error is returned. On full success ceph_set_cached_acl(inode, type, acl) is called and 0 is returned; that call only caches the ACL when the XATTR_SHARED cap is held, so success does not guarantee the ACL is cached. The temporary xattr buffer is always freed; the caller keeps ownership of acl (no reference is taken or dropped).
note: Corrected: caching on success is conditional inside ceph_set_cached_acl; DEFAULT/non-dir/NULL returns 0 without caching.

name: write_folio_nounlock
prose: Precondition: folio is a locked folio of a ceph inode's mapping; wbc is the writeback control (may be NULL on the error path, where a local one is substituted). Postcondition: the folio stays locked on every path. Returns -EIO immediately if the inode is shut down. Returns 0 doing nothing else if the folio has no snap context (not dirty). If the folio's snap context seq is greater than the oldest context's seq (the folio is newer than the oldest writeable context, so not writeable now) it WARNs unless the caller is in PF_MEMALLOC, redirties the folio, drops the oldest-context ref and returns 0. If the folio position is at or beyond the inode size it calls folio_invalidate on the whole folio and returns 0 (no write is submitted). Otherwise it clips the length to i_size (rounded up to the fscrypt block for encrypted inodes), increments fsc->writeback_count (setting write_congested above the threshold) and builds an OSD write request: if request creation fails it redirties the folio, decrements the count and returns PTR_ERR(req); if the inode is encrypted and encryption of the bounce page fails it redirties the folio, ends writeback, puts the request, decrements the count and returns that error. Otherwise it starts writeback, submits and waits for the request, updates write metrics, frees the bounce page and puts the request; if the result err is -ERESTARTSYS it redirties the folio, ends writeback, decrements the count and returns -ERESTARTSYS without touching the page snap context; on any other error it sets the mapping error (and the blocklisted flag for -EBLOCKLISTED) and increments wbc->pages_skipped, and on success err is set to 0. In both of these cases it then detaches the folio's private snap context, ends writeback, drops the cap wrbuffer refs and the page's snap-context reference, decrements writeback_count (clearing write_congested below the low threshold) and returns err (0 on success or the negative error).
note: Slice truncated the function tail (ends before request submission); prose written from full source. Fixed newer/older snapc direction.

name: __send_flush_snap
prose: Precondition: inode, session and capsnap are valid; capsnap is kept alive by the caller (which holds a reference) and the caller does not hold ci->i_ceph_lock (the caller drops it around the call); the function takes no lock itself. Postcondition: builds a cap_msg_args from capsnap (op CEPH_CAP_OP_FLUSHSNAP, follows, flush tid, sizes, times, mode, uid/gid, inline data, oldest_flush_tid and mseq as passed); allocates a message with ceph_msg_new(CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_CAPS, ..., GFP_NOFS): if the allocation fails returns -ENOMEM and sends nothing; otherwise encodes the message, sends it on session->s_con and returns 0. It takes or releases no locks or references, and does not modify capsnap or the inode.
note: Prose fixed; inline function, no contract.

name: __ceph_flush_snaps
prose: Precondition: the caller holds ci->i_ceph_lock and session is a valid session reference held by the caller. Postcondition: returns void with ci->i_ceph_lock held again (it is dropped around each message send and re-taken). First pass: walks ci->i_cap_snaps from the head, stopping at the first capsnap that has dirty_pages or writing set; an earlier capsnap whose cap_flush.tid is already non-zero is skipped, and otherwise (BUG_ON if need_flush is not set) it is assigned a new tid ++mdsc->last_cap_flush_tid under cap_dirty_lock, appended to mdsc->cap_flush_list and ci->i_cap_flush_list, ci is added to session->s_cap_flushing if not already on a flushing list, and the first/last tid range is recorded. It then clears CEPH_I_FLUSH_SNAPS on ci. Second pass: for each queued flush with tid in [first_tid, last_tid] in order, if ci->i_auth_cap is NULL or belongs to another session it stops; otherwise it takes a reference on the capsnap, drops i_ceph_lock, sends the flush-snap message via __send_flush_snap (an error, i.e. -ENOMEM, is only logged and not retried), puts the capsnap reference and retakes the lock. Not every ready capsnap is necessarily sent (send may fail, or the loop may stop because the auth cap changed), and capsnaps after a dirty/writing one are not flushed.
note: Clarified that CEPH_I_FLUSH_SNAPS is cleared even if sends later fail/abort.

name: ceph_flush_snaps
prose: Precondition: ci is a valid inode info and the caller holds an inode reference; the caller does NOT hold ci->i_ceph_lock; psession is NULL or points to a session pointer (possibly NULL) whose reference the caller holds. Postcondition: always returns void with ci->i_ceph_lock released. If CEPH_I_FLUSH_SNAPS is not set, or ci has no auth cap, nothing is flushed. Otherwise, if the passed session is for a different MDS than the auth cap's, its reference is dropped and the correct session is looked up (reference taken) under mdsc->mutex and the check repeated; once a session matches, CEPH_I_KICK_FLUSH (if set) causes __kick_flushing_caps first, then __ceph_flush_snaps(ci, session) is invoked. Session reference handling: if psession is non-NULL, *psession is set to the current session (reference transferred back to the caller, possibly NULL or a newly looked up one, even if nothing was flushed); if psession is NULL the session reference is dropped. Finally, under mdsc->snap_flush_lock ci is removed from the snap-flush queue (list_del_init) in every case, and if it was queued the inode reference is released with iput.
note: Corrected: queue removal and iput occur on all paths, session ownership via psession.

name: ceph_check_caps
prose: Precondition: ci is a valid inode info, the caller holds an inode reference and does NOT hold ci->i_ceph_lock; flags is a combination of CHECK_CAPS_* bits. The function takes no session argument and holds no session reference on entry. Postcondition: returns void with ci->i_ceph_lock released and any session reference it took internally dropped (every iteration puts the previously held session, and the final put releases the last one). If CEPH_I_ASYNC_CREATE is set it sets CEPH_I_ASYNC_CHECK_CAPS, releases the lock and returns immediately without reconciling caps or sending any message (no session reference is held at that point). Otherwise it adds CHECK_CAPS_FLUSH if CEPH_I_FLUSH is set and CHECK_CAPS_FLUSH_FORCE if CEPH_I_FLUSH_FORCE is set, computes wanted/used/retain caps, may try a non-blocking invalidate of cached pages (queuing an invalidate if it fails), then scans ci->i_caps in increasing mds order (skipping non-auth caps with CHECK_CAPS_AUTHONLY): for any cap needing action (completed revocation, forced flush, new max_size requested, size reporting, dirty caps to flush, snap flush pending, wanted caps change, or issued caps beyond retain) it takes a reference on that cap's session, first kicking flushing caps and flushing snaps and restarting the scan if the auth cap has CEPH_I_KICK_FLUSH or CEPH_I_FLUSH_SNAPS set, otherwise marks dirty caps flushing, drops i_ceph_lock, sends an update cap message via __send_cap, retakes the lock and restarts the scan. When no more caps need messages it may requeue the inode on the delayed-cap list, releases the lock, drops the session reference, and queues writeback (if a Fb revoke is blocked by wrbuffer refs) and/or invalidation if flagged.
note: Fixed: no session parameter; the async-create early return holds no session reference.

name: try_flush_caps
prose: Precondition: inode is a valid ceph inode and the caller does NOT hold ci->i_ceph_lock; ptid points to writable u64 storage. Postcondition: takes ci->i_ceph_lock once and always releases it before returning (it is never re-taken after being dropped, apart from internal re-checks while held); always stores a value into *ptid and returns a cap bitmask. If ci->i_dirty_caps is non-zero and ci->i_auth_cap is set: if the auth cap's session is not yet open (state < CEPH_MDS_SESSION_OPEN) it returns 0 with *ptid = 0 and sends nothing; otherwise, if CEPH_I_KICK_FLUSH or CEPH_I_FLUSH_SNAPS is set it kicks flushing caps and/or flushes snaps (under the lock) and re-evaluates; then it marks the dirty caps as flushing with __mark_caps_flushing (assigning flush_tid), drops the lock, sends a CEPH_CAP_OP_FLUSH cap message with the SYNC flag via __send_cap, and returns the bitmask of caps that were dirty (now flushing) with *ptid set to the new flush tid. Otherwise (no dirty caps or no auth cap) it sets *ptid to the tid of the last entry of ci->i_cap_flush_list (and sets that entry's wake flag) or 0 if the list is empty, and returns ci->i_flushing_caps (possibly 0). No references are taken or released.
note: Fixed: lock taken once, never reacquired after drop; clarified retry and wake flag.

name: handle_cap_grant
prose: Precondition: handle_cap_grant(inode, session, cap, grant, xattr_buf, extra_info): the caller holds session->s_mutex, ci->i_ceph_lock, and (for a CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT grant) session->s_mdsc->snap_rwsem for reading; cap belongs to inode (the auth cap or, for a non-import grant, possibly a non-auth cap), grant is a decoded mds caps message, xattr_buf is the buffer holding the xattr blob (used only if a newer xattr version is accepted), and extra_info holds the decoded ancillary data. Postcondition: returns void; it releases ci->i_ceph_lock and session->s_mutex on return and, if grant->op is IMPORT, also releases snap_rwsem (read). While under the lock: if the cap generation was stale, cap->issued and cap->implemented are reset to CEPH_CAP_PIN; if the message seq is not newer than cap->seq the cap's seq and its issued caps are retained (newcaps |= cap->issued); cap->cap_gen is set to the current session generation and cap->seq to the message seq; mode/uid/gid, nlink, xattr blob (taking a ref on xattr_buf and dropping the old blob when version is newer), times, dir stats, layout (the replaced old pool_ns is returned to the caller through extra_info->pool_ns), file size/truncate state, max_size on the auth cap, and inline version are updated from the grant according to which caps (newcaps) and extra_info->issued allow; cap->issued becomes newcaps (kept within cap->implemented, which only gains bits; BUG_ON otherwise). A revocation of cached or buffered caps may queue writeback or invalidation and set CEPH_I_FLUSH_FORCE when a revoke ack must be deferred; a revoke op otherwise clears cap->mds_wanted and forces a flush ack. After unlocking it may fill inline data, queue vmtruncate/writeback/invalidate, invalidate aliases for a deleted inode (nlink 0), wake ci->i_cap_wq waiters, and finally call ceph_check_caps (auth-only or all caps, with NOINVAL, plus FLUSH_FORCE for a revoke) when needed.
note: Slice cut the function head (the excerpt starts mid-function); real name is handle_cap_grant (name taken from source file). Prose rewritten with lock set (s_mutex, i_ceph_lock, snap_rwsem on import) and deferred revoke handling.

name: handle_cap_flush_ack
prose: Precondition: the caller holds ci->i_ceph_lock (it is always released before return) and a reference on inode; flush_tid is the tid acknowledged by the MDS, m the ack message, session and cap valid. Postcondition: returns void with ci->i_ceph_lock released. Scans ci->i_cap_flush_list: for the entry whose tid equals flush_tid, cleaned is set to its caps (even if it is a capsnap); capsnap entries (is_capsnap) are otherwise skipped and stay attached; every non-capsnap entry with tid <= flush_tid is detached from ci (and later from mdsc) and freed with ceph_free_cap_flush after the lock is dropped, whether or not an entry with exactly flush_tid exists; for each later non-capsnap entry its caps are removed from cleaned, and the scan stops once cleaned is empty. If nothing was detached and cleaned is 0 nothing else changes. Otherwise ci->i_flushing_caps drops the cleaned caps; under mdsc->cap_dirty_lock the detached entries are detached from the mdsc lists; if ci->i_flushing_caps is then 0, mdsc->num_cap_flushing is decremented, ci is removed from the session's flushing list if its flush list is empty, and if ci->i_dirty_caps is also 0 the head snap context is put and cleared when i_wr_ref and i_wrbuffer_ref_head are both 0 and the caller's inode reference is dropped with iput at the end (BUG_ON checks on i_dirty_item/i_head_snapc). After unlocking, waiters on ci->i_cap_wq and/or mdsc->cap_flushing_wq are woken as reported by the detach helpers.
note: Fixed: non-capsnap entries with tid <= flush_tid are removed even without an exact match; capsnaps are skipped; iput only when no dirty caps remain.

name: ceph_make_fpos
prose: Precondition: none; high and off are arbitrary unsigned 32-bit values (high << 28 fits in 60 bits). Postcondition: returns the loff_t value (((loff_t)high << 28) | (loff_t)off), additionally OR-ed with HASH_ORDER (0xff << 52, i.e. 0xFF0000000000000) if and only if hash_order is true. Pure: no memory, locks or references involved.
note: Prose precondition dropped (no overflow: high < 2^32 so shifted value < 2^60); HASH_ORDER is 0xff<<52.

name: __dir_lease_check
prose: Precondition: __dir_lease_check(dentry, lwc): dentry is a ceph dentry whose d_lock is held by the caller (as it is called from the lease walk), its parent is valid unless it is a root, and lwc points to a walk control with dir_lease_ttl and expire_dir_lease set. Postcondition: let r = __dir_lease_try_check(dentry), which trylocks the parent's ci->i_ceph_lock (releasing it before returning) and sets di->lease_shared_gen to 0 whenever it finds the dir lease not valid (r <= 0). If r == -EBUSY the function returns KEEP. If r > 0 (valid dir lease): it returns STOP if jiffies is still before di->time + lwc->dir_lease_ttl; else KEEP if lwc->expire_dir_lease is false; else TOUCH if dentry->d_lockref.count > 0 or CEPH_DENTRY_REFERENCED is set in di->flags; else it sets di->lease_shared_gen = 0 and returns DELETE. If r is 0 or any negative value other than -EBUSY it returns DELETE (no expiry check). Only di->lease_shared_gen is modified (by the callee or here); no locks or references are acquired or retained and the dentry is not otherwise changed.
note: Fixed: DELETE also for r<=0 without expiry test; lease_shared_gen is written; KEEP/STOP/TOUCH/DELETE conditions enumerated. Slice's named function is the prototype only; named after __dir_lease_check, source line 1755 of dir.c.

name: ceph_readdir
prose: Precondition: file is an open ceph directory file (file->private_data is its struct ceph_dir_file_info), ctx is a valid dir_context and the caller holds the directory's inode lock for iteration as usual for iterate; no ceph spinlocks are held. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if CEPH_F_ATEND is set. Otherwise it first emits '.' (pos 0) and '..' (pos 1), advancing ctx->pos to 1 and 2; if dir_emit refuses an entry (caller's buffer full) it returns 0 with ctx->pos left at that entry's position, and the same 'return 0 on full buffer' applies to every later emission. It then returns the negative errno of ceph_fscrypt_prepare_readdir if that fails. If the dcache can be used (mount options allow it, not a snapdir, dir is complete and ordered, Fs cap held) it calls __dcache_readdir and returns its result unless that is -EAGAIN, in which case it falls through. Normal path: when the buffered reply does not cover ctx->pos it drops the previous reply (dfi->last_readdir) and sends a READDIR (or LSSNAP) request to the auth MDS for the current frag, returning -errno on failure of request creation (PTR_ERR), reply-buffer allocation, kzalloc of r_path2 (-ENOMEM), encoding of the encrypted last name, or the request itself (in each case the request reference taken here is dropped), or the note_last_dentry error (after dropping the reply). It then emits the buffered entries from ctx->pos onward, setting ctx->pos to each emitted entry's offset and then incrementing it; it returns -EIO (dropping the reply) if an entry's offset is below ctx->pos or an entry has no inode; if dir_emit refuses an entry it returns 0 with dfi->last_readdir retained so the next call resumes. When the buffered entries are exhausted the reply reference is dropped and it moves on to further requests for the same frag or the next frag; at the end of the last frag it sets CEPH_F_ATEND, marks the directory complete (and records the readdir-cache size in i_size) if no dentries were released during the whole readdir, and returns 0. On every return no spinlock is held; a request or reply reference remains held only in dfi->last_readdir when stopped by a full buffer.
note: Fixed: full-buffer returns 0 keeping dfi->last_readdir; -ENOMEM and -EIO paths listed; no claim that all refs are released.

name: ceph_fh_to_parent
prose: Precondition: sb is a ceph superblock; fid points to a file handle whose raw data (at least fh_len 32-bit words when the confh branch is taken) is a struct ceph_nfs_snapfh when fh_type is FILEID_BTRFS_WITH_PARENT and a struct ceph_nfs_confh otherwise. Postcondition: if fh_type == FILEID_BTRFS_WITH_PARENT it returns __snapfh_to_dentry(sb, sfh, true) directly with no check on fh_len, and every error pointer or dentry it returns propagates; otherwise it returns NULL if fh_type is not FILEID_INO32_GEN_PARENT, and NULL if fh_len is smaller than sizeof(struct ceph_nfs_confh) / BYTES_PER_U32; otherwise it returns __get_parent(sb, NULL, cfh->ino), except that when that result is exactly ERR_PTR(-ENOENT) it is replaced by __fh_to_dentry(sb, cfh->parent_ino); any other error pointer (MDS or allocation errors such as -ESTALE, -ENOMEM) or dentry from the callees is returned unchanged. On success the caller receives a referenced dentry; this function takes no locks.
note: Fixed: fh_len check applies only to the FILEID_INO32_GEN_PARENT branch.

name: get_rd_wr_caps
prose: Precondition: src_filp and dst_filp are valid open ceph files, dst_endoff is the end offset of the destination range, and src_got and dst_got point to writable ints; the caller holds no cap references on either inode for this call. Postcondition: on success it returns a positive value (the result of ceph_try_get_caps, 1) with *dst_got holding the references acquired for CEPH_CAP_FILE_WR (want FILE_BUFFER) on the destination inode and *src_got holding references for CEPH_CAP_FILE_RD (want FILE_SHARED) on the source inode; the caller must later release both sets with ceph_put_cap_refs. On failure it returns a negative errno and holds no cap references on either inode: it fails with the error of the first ceph_get_caps on dst; otherwise, if the non-blocking ceph_try_get_caps on src fails or returns 0 (or an error), the dst references are dropped and, on the first attempt, the src caps are obtained with the blocking ceph_get_caps (its error, if any, is returned), then dropped, and the whole sequence is retried once; if the non-blocking src attempt fails again, the dst references are dropped and the error is returned, with a ret of 0 (would block) converted to -EAGAIN.
note: Real function, not a dropped non-function: slice head is cut but get_rd_wr_caps is a real function in file.c; success return is >0 and both ref sets are held.

name: try_prep_async_create
prose: Real function name: try_prep_async_create(dir, dentry, lo, pino) (the slice starts mid-function, so its name does not appear in the slice; try_get_deleg_ino_and_caps is not a name in the source). Precondition: dir is a valid ceph directory inode, dentry a valid dentry of it, lo points to writable struct ceph_file_layout storage and pino to writable u64 storage; the caller does not hold dir's ci->i_ceph_lock (it is taken and released inside). Postcondition: returns either want = (CEPH_CAP_FILE_EXCL | CEPH_CAP_DIR_CREATE) or 0. It returns 0 (releasing the lock, taking no references and leaving *pino and *lo untouched) if dir has no auth cap, the auth session has no delegated inode numbers, the cached layout is not valid, the issued caps do not include all of want, the dentry is in lookup and the directory is not complete, the dentry is not in lookup and its lease_shared_gen differs from the directory's i_shared_gen, or no delegated inode number can be obtained. In the in-lookup/complete-directory case it first sets di->lease_shared_gen to the directory's shared gen (under dentry->d_lock) even if it later returns 0. On success it removes one inode number from the session's delegated set and stores it in *pino, takes cap references for want on dir (the caller must release them with ceph_put_cap_refs), copies the cached layout to *lo with lo->pool_ns set to a new reference on the cached pool namespace string (possibly NULL) that the caller must put, and returns want, with the lock released.
note: Slice head cut; the packet name try_get_deleg_ino_and_caps does not exist in the source; real name is try_prep_async_create, which is not in the slice.

name: ceph_fill_inode
prose: Precondition: ceph_fill_inode(inode, locked_page, iinfo, dirinfo, session, cap_fmode, caps_reservation): the caller holds mdsc->snap_rwsem (lockdep_assert_held; for reading) and does NOT hold ci->i_ceph_lock, which this function takes and releases itself; iinfo/iinfo->in hold the decoded inode and cap info, session is the reply's MDS session, dirinfo may be NULL, locked_page may be NULL, cap_fmode is a file mode or negative, and caps_reservation covers a cap allocation. Postcondition: returns 0 on success; otherwise a negative errno with no lock held. If the inode is not I_NEW and its type changed or its char/block rdev changed it returns -ESTALE before any change; if the reply carries caps for a non-snapshot inode and ceph_get_cap fails it returns -ENOMEM before any change. Otherwise the inode is updated under ci->i_ceph_lock from the reply according to the version comparison and which caps are held (mode, uid/gid, btime, blkbits, nlink, times, dir stats, layout including pool namespace, size/truncate state, max_size on the auth cap, dir rstats, xattr blob when newer, i_version, ops vectors by file type, inline data version and cap mode touch); a capability is added with ceph_add_cap (consuming the preallocated cap) for a non-snapshot inode, or i_snap_caps is ORed for a snapshot inode, and an empty complete directory may be marked complete. For symlinks the lock is dropped to build the symlink target: a failure to decode an encrypted symlink returns its negative error and a failed kstrndup returns -ENOMEM, in which case the inode is left partially updated but all temporary references (the unused cap, old/new xattr blob buffers and the replaced pool-namespace string) are released. After unlocking it registers the fscache cookie, may fill inline data, wake cap waiters, queue a vmtruncate, fill the fragtree for directories and the dirfrag when dirinfo is given. A failed xattr blob allocation is only logged and leaves the blob NULL while the xattr version is still updated.
note: Slice cut the function head; prose fixed: caller holds snap_rwsem (not i_ceph_lock), which is taken/released internally; -ESTALE, -ENOMEM paths added.

name: __update_dentry_lease
prose: Precondition: the caller holds dentry->d_lock; dir is the parent ceph directory inode; lease, session and from_time describe an MDS reply lease; old_lease_session points to a struct ceph_mds_session pointer the caller initialised (to NULL) and will put after dropping locks. Postcondition: returns void and cannot fail. If ceph_snap(dir) != CEPH_NOSNAP it returns at once with nothing changed. Otherwise, in every remaining case, di->flags gets CEPH_DENTRY_PRIMARY_LINK set or cleared according to lease->mask and di->lease_shared_gen is set to the directory's i_shared_gen. If lease->mask lacks CEPH_LEASE_VALID it then touches the dir lease (__ceph_dentry_dir_lease_touch) and returns, leaving the other lease fields unchanged. If di->lease_gen equals session->s_cap_gen and the computed ttl is before di->time (a newer lease is already held) it returns with the lease fields unchanged. Otherwise: if di->lease_session is non-NULL and differs from session, that old session pointer (and its reference) is moved into *old_lease_session for the caller to put and di->lease_session becomes NULL; then if di->lease_session is NULL it is set to session with a new reference taken via ceph_get_mds_session (if di->lease_session already equals session no new reference is taken); di->lease_gen, lease_seq, lease_renew_after (half of the duration), lease_renew_from (0) and di->time (the ttl) are set from the lease, and the dentry is touched on the lease list.
note: Fixed: flags and lease_shared_gen are updated before the early returns; session ref only taken if di->lease_session is NULL.

name: ceph_fill_trace
prose: Real function (not a non-function): ceph_fill_trace(sb, req) fills the VFS state (parent directory inode, target inode, dentry and dentry lease) from the parsed MDS reply req->r_reply_info; the slice head is cut so the name is not in the slice. Precondition: req holds a parsed reply (rinfo) with r_session set; the caller (handle_reply) has set req->r_target_inode when rinfo->head->is_target; for the dentry paths req->r_parent, r_dentry and r_old_dentry(_dir) are consistent with the reply and the PARENT_LOCKED flag says whether the parent is locked; the caller holds mdsc->snap_rwsem as ceph_fill_inode requires. Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno. If the reply has neither a target nor a dentry it returns 0, first calling ceph_invalidate_dir_request when the result is 0 and req->r_parent is set. If is_dentry: the reply directory is looked up with ceph_get_reply_dir (its error is returned) and filled via ceph_fill_inode (its error returned); for a LOOKUPNAME on a locked parent that is not aborted a dentry for the (decrypted) name is found or allocated and stored in req->r_dentry (-ENOMEM, or the filename buffer/decrypt error, on failure). If is_target: ceph_fill_inode is applied to req->r_target_inode (fmode only if not aborted, not async and result 0); on error it sets req->r_target_inode to NULL, discards the inode (discard_new_inode if I_NEW, else iput) and returns that error; on success a new inode is unlocked. Then, depending on flags, dentry and lease handling runs: a null reply dentry deletes a positive dentry or adds a negative one and updates the lease; a target attaches the inode (splice_dentry error returned, -EINVAL if there is no target inode in hand), handles renames by d_move, d_invalidates a mismatched inode, and updates the dentry lease; LOOKUPSNAP/MKSNAP on a locked parent splices the snapdir dentry (error returned); otherwise the lease is updated carefully on an unlocked parent. On exit any extra reference on parent_dir obtained from ceph_get_reply_dir (when it differs from req->r_parent) is dropped with iput; on error paths the target inode has already been released as described, other state may be partially updated.
note: Real function; slice head cut (name absent from slice). Prose describes return paths.

name: ceph_setattr
prose: Real function (not a non-function): ceph_setattr(idmap, dentry, attr) is the inode_operations setattr; slice head cut so the name is not in the slice. Precondition: dentry is valid with a valid inode, attr is a valid iattr whose ia_valid says what to change; the caller holds the inode lock as for notify_change. Postcondition: returns -EROFS if the inode is a snapshot inode, -ESTALE if the inode is shut down, the error of fscrypt_prepare_setattr or setattr_prepare if either fails, -EFBIG if ATTR_SIZE is set and attr->ia_size exceeds max(i_size, fsc->max_file_size), and -EDQUOT if ATTR_SIZE is set and ceph_quota_is_max_bytes_exceeded for the new size; otherwise it calls __ceph_setattr (which applies the changes locally under exclusive caps or via a SETATTR MDS request) and, if that returned a non-negative value and ATTR_MODE is set, applies posix_acl_chmod with attr->ia_mode and returns its result; the result is __ceph_setattr's value or the posix_acl_chmod value, 0 meaning success. It takes and releases no locks and holds no references of its own.
note: Real function; the old prose described __ceph_setattr/a request, not ceph_setattr.

name: ceph_lock
prose: Real function name is ceph_lock(file, cmd, fl) (the packet name ceph_fcntl does not exist in the source; the slice cuts the head of ceph_lock, so the name is absent from the slice). Precondition: file is an open ceph file, fl a valid file_lock, cmd an fcntl lock command (F_GETLK, F_SETLK or F_SETLKW style); the caller holds no ceph locks. Postcondition: returns -ENOLCK if FL_POSIX is not set in fl->c.flc_flags and -ESTALE if the inode is shut down, in both cases with no side effects. If CEPH_I_ERROR_FILELOCK is set on the inode it returns -EIO, and if the request is a SETFILELOCK-type unlock it first calls posix_lock_file(file, fl, NULL) to drop the local lock. For a non-GETLK unlock request it first calls try_unlock_file, which unlocks locally with FL_EXISTS: if the result is <= 0 it is returned and nothing is sent to the MDS (0 when there was nothing to unlock and the caller did not set FL_EXISTS, -ENOENT when FL_EXISTS was set by the caller, or another local error), and only a positive result continues. Then ceph_lock_message is called (GETLK for F_GETLK, SETFILELOCK otherwise, with wait set only for SETLKW and non-unlock): if it fails its negative error is returned (it may have taken the i_filelock_ref reference attached to the lock, released by fl_release_private); if it succeeds for a GETLK it returns 0 with fl filled in with the conflicting lock; if it succeeds for a SETFILELOCK that is not an unlock, the lock is also applied locally with posix_lock_file: its failure is returned after undoing the remote lock via a CEPH_LOCK_UNLOCK ceph_lock_message, and otherwise 0 is returned. ci->i_ceph_lock is taken and released briefly only to read the error flag.
note: Real function is ceph_lock (packet name ceph_fcntl is absent from the source); head cut. Prose rewritten with try_unlock_file semantics.

name: register_session
prose: Precondition: register_session(mdsc, mds): the caller holds mdsc->mutex (the sessions array is modified), mds >= 0, and there is no session already stored at mdsc->sessions[mds] (it would be overwritten without release). Postcondition: returns ERR_PTR(-EIO) if the mount state is CEPH_MOUNT_FENCE_IO, ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) if mds >= mdsc->mdsmap->possible_max_rank, ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if the session allocation or the enlarging of the sessions array fails (the new session is freed and mdsc is unchanged on failure). Otherwise it first enlarges mdsc->sessions, if mds >= mdsc->max_sessions, to the next power of two above mds (copying the old pointers and freeing the old array), then allocates and initialises a new session in state CEPH_MDS_SESSION_NEW, stores it in mdsc->sessions[mds], increments mdsc->num_sessions, sets its refcount to 2 (one for the sessions array, one for the caller, who must put it with ceph_put_mds_session), opens its connection to the MDS address from the mdsmap and returns it. Note the array enlargement is retained even if a later step... none can fail after the allocation, so a successful return always means all effects were applied.
note: Slice head cut (the packet starts after the function head); added missing precondition mdsc->mutex held and sessions[mds] empty.

name: check_caps_flush
prose: Precondition: mdsc is a valid ceph_mds_client and want_flush_tid is any u64; the caller does not hold mdsc->cap_dirty_lock. Postcondition: takes and releases mdsc->cap_dirty_lock, modifies nothing, and returns 1 if mdsc->cap_flush_list is empty or its first entry has a tid greater than want_flush_tid (all flushes up to want_flush_tid have completed), and returns 0 if the list is non-empty and its first entry's tid is less than or equal to want_flush_tid.
note: Pointer/list function, no scalar contract.

name: ceph_flush_session_cap_releases
prose: Precondition: mdsc is a valid ceph_mds_client and session a valid ceph_mds_session; no ceph locks are required. Postcondition: returns void. If mdsc->stopping is set it returns immediately without taking a session reference and without queueing anything. Otherwise it takes a reference on session and calls queue_work on mdsc->fsc->cap_wq with session->s_cap_release_work: if the work was queued (it was not already pending) the reference is owned by the queued work and is dropped later by ceph_cap_release_work; if the work was already pending (queue_work returned false) the reference just taken is dropped before returning. No cap releases are sent directly by this function.
note: Clarified stopping check precedes the reference and that already-pending work drops the new reference.

name: handle_reply
prose: Precondition: handle_reply(session, msg): msg is a received MDS reply message whose front buffer may be of any length; the caller holds none of mdsc->mutex, session->s_mutex, mdsc->snap_rwsem or req->r_fill_mutex (all taken and released inside). Postcondition: returns void. If msg->front is shorter than struct ceph_mds_reply_head it logs, dumps the message and returns with no other effect. It then looks up the request by msg->hdr.tid under mdsc->mutex taking a reference; if there is none it returns. If the request's session differs from session, or the reply is a duplicate unsafe or safe reply, or an unsafe reply arrives after a safe one, it logs and returns without recording a result (after dropping the looked-up request reference). A safe reply sets GOT_SAFE and unregisters the request (completing safe_umount_waiters if stopping and no requests remain); if an unsafe reply had already been handled, a safe reply then returns without recording anything further. An unsafe reply sets GOT_UNSAFE and links the request on the session's s_unsafe list. Otherwise the reply is parsed (parse_reply_info); on success a target inode is found or created (ceph_get_inode; its error becomes the error), the snap trace is applied under snap_rwsem (a failure there sets close_sessions so all sessions are closed after unlocking) and the trace is filled with ceph_fill_trace (plus ceph_readdir_prepopulate for a successful READDIR/LSSNAP reply). Finally, under mdsc->mutex, if the request was not aborted it records either r_err = the negative error (corrupt reply or any failure above) or, on success, r_reply = a new reference to msg with GOT_RESULT set; if it was aborted neither field is set. On every path after the lookup it drops the request reference taken by lookup_get_request, wakes the waiter with complete_request on the paths that recorded or tried to record a result (not on wrong-session, duplicate or safe-after-unsafe returns), updates the metadata metrics, and calls ceph_mdsc_close_sessions(mdsc) last if close_sessions was set.
note: Added safe-after-unsafe path (no result recorded) and wrong-session/dup returns; the function takes mdsc->mutex itself.

name: chrdev_open
prose: Precondition: inode is a character-device inode (inode->i_rdev names the device) and filp is the file being opened on it; the caller holds no cdev_lock. Postcondition: returns 0, -ENXIO, or the nonzero value returned by the device's own open method. It returns -ENXIO if inode->i_cdev is not yet bound and kobj_lookup(cdev_map, i_rdev) finds no registered device, or if cdev_get on the (existing or just bound) cdev fails because its owner module is going away; in these cases filp is unchanged and no reference is held. If inode->i_cdev was unset (and no one else bound it meanwhile) it is bound to the looked-up cdev and the inode is added to that cdev's list (a persistent effect that stays even if the open later fails); if another task bound it in the meantime the extra cdev reference from the lookup is dropped. It then takes fops_get(p->ops): if that fails it returns -ENXIO after dropping the cdev reference with filp unchanged. Otherwise replace_fops(filp, fops) installs the device's file_operations in filp (filp holds the fops reference, the previous f_op reference is released); if filp->f_op->open is non-NULL it is called and its non-zero result is returned after dropping the cdev reference (filp->f_op stays replaced); if the open method is NULL or returns 0 the function returns 0 and the cdev reference taken here is retained for the open file (released when the file is released).
note: Added i_cdev binding side effect, the fops_get failure path and exact reference behaviour.

name: coda_flags_to_cflags
prose: Precondition: none; flags is an unsigned short of open flags. Postcondition: returns an unsigned short in which C_O_READ (0x001) is set exactly when (flags & O_ACCMODE) is O_RDONLY or O_RDWR, C_O_WRITE (0x002) exactly when it is O_WRONLY or O_RDWR (so an access mode of 3 sets neither), C_O_TRUNC (0x010), C_O_CREAT (0x200) and C_O_EXCL (0x100) are set exactly when O_TRUNC, O_CREAT and O_EXCL respectively are set in flags, and no other bits are set. Pure: no memory, locks or references.
contract: /*@ requires 1; ensures result == (((((flags & O_ACCMODE) == O_RDONLY) || ((flags & O_ACCMODE) == O_RDWR)) ? C_O_READ : 0) | ((((flags & O_ACCMODE) == O_RDWR) || ((flags & O_ACCMODE) == O_WRONLY)) ? C_O_WRITE : 0) | (((flags & O_TRUNC) != 0) ? C_O_TRUNC : 0) | (((flags & O_CREAT) != 0) ? C_O_CREAT : 0) | (((flags & O_EXCL) != 0) ? C_O_EXCL : 0)); */
note: Previous contract parsed as (result == A) | B (precedence); whole right-hand side now parenthesised; O_ACCMODE==3 is handled by the code (no R/W bits), so no precondition is needed.

name: coda_iattr_to_vattr
prose: Precondition: iattr and vattr point to valid, writable objects of their types; they do not alias. Postcondition: returns void. First every field of *vattr is initialised: va_mode, va_uid, va_gid, va_size, va_fileid, va_gen, va_bytes, va_nlink, va_blocksize and va_rdev to -1 (cast to their types), va_atime, va_mtime and va_ctime (both tv_sec and tv_nsec) to -1, va_type to C_VNON and va_flags to 0. Then, according to iattr->ia_valid, only the fields whose bit is set are overwritten: ATTR_MODE sets va_mode = iattr->ia_mode; ATTR_UID sets va_uid = from_kuid(&init_user_ns, iattr->ia_uid); ATTR_GID sets va_gid likewise; ATTR_SIZE sets va_size = iattr->ia_size; ATTR_ATIME, ATTR_MTIME and ATTR_CTIME set the corresponding timestamps with timespec64_to_coda(). va_type stays C_VNON and va_flags stays 0 whatever ia_valid is; iattr is not modified; no locks or references are involved.
note: Field list made precise; no change of substance.

name: venus_statfs
prose: Precondition: dentry is a valid dentry of a coda superblock and sfs points to writable struct kstatfs storage. Postcondition: allocates an upcall message; if the allocation fails it returns -ENOMEM (no upcall is sent, sfs unchanged). Otherwise it performs a synchronous CODA_STATFS upcall to Venus via coda_upcall on the superblock's channel; if that returns 0 it sets sfs->f_blocks, f_bfree, f_bavail, f_files and f_ffree from Venus's reply and returns 0; if it returns an error (-ENXIO when Venus is not running, -ENOMEM for the request allocation, -EINTR when interrupted, or the negated Venus result) that error is returned and sfs is left unchanged. The upcall buffer is always freed with kvfree before returning once it was allocated; the function holds no locks of its own and keeps no references.
note: Added -ENOMEM from the buffer allocation (UPARG).

name: venus_access_intent
prose: Precondition: sb is a valid coda superblock, fid points to a valid CodaFid, access_intent_supported points to a bool that records whether Venus supports chunked access, count, ppos and type describe the access, and type is a CODA_ACCESS_TYPE_* value. Postcondition: if *access_intent_supported is false and type is neither CODA_ACCESS_TYPE_READ_FINISH nor CODA_ACCESS_TYPE_WRITE_FINISH it returns 0 without sending anything. Otherwise it allocates the message, returning -ENOMEM if that fails, and sends a CODA_ACCESS_INTENT upcall: for the two FINISH types the upcall is asynchronous (outsize NULL), and the message buffer is NOT freed here when the upcall succeeds (ownership passes to the queued request) but IS freed when it fails; for other types the upcall is synchronous and the buffer is always freed. If the upcall's result is -EOPNOTSUPP, *access_intent_supported is set to false and 0 is returned; otherwise the result of the upcall is returned (0 on success, -ENXIO if Venus is not running, -ENOMEM, -EINTR, or the negated Venus error for synchronous upcalls).
note: Added the allocation failure and exact ownership/EOPNOTSUPP behaviour.

name: coda_waitfor_upcall
prose: Precondition: coda_waitfor_upcall(vcp, req): the caller holds vcp->vc_mutex and req is a queued upcall request (on vcp->vc_pending) for the current task. Postcondition: returns void with vcp->vc_mutex held again (it is released while sleeping and re-acquired every iteration). It blocks all signals except SIGKILL, SIGSTOP and SIGINT (coda_block_signals) while waiting on req->uc_sleep; it sleeps (interruptibly if CODA_INTERRUPTIBLE(req), else uninterruptibly) in steps of one second while signals are blocked, until req->uc_flags has CODA_REQ_WRITE (reply) or CODA_REQ_ABORT set, or a signal is pending after the timeout has elapsed and signals have been unblocked, in which case req is removed from its list (list_del(&req->uc_chain)) and the wait ends. After coda_timeout seconds, if the request is interruptible, the saved signal mask is restored early so signals can interrupt; the original mask is always restored before return (once, on the early path or at the end). The wait queue entry is removed and the task state is TASK_RUNNING on return. The reason the wait ended is visible only in req->uc_flags and signal_pending(current), not in a return value.
note: Clarified timeout/signal semantics: list_del only on signal; mutex dropped and retaken.

name: coda_upcall
prose: Real function is coda_upcall(vcp, inSize, outSize, buffer) (the slice only contains its prototype, the body is later in upcall.c). Precondition: the caller does not hold vcp->vc_mutex; buffer is a complete input message of inSize bytes allocated by the caller (alloc_upcall) with a valid inputArgs header; outSize is NULL for an asynchronous request or points to an int holding the expected reply size (0 meaning inSize) for a synchronous one. Postcondition: takes vcp->vc_mutex and releases it before returning. If vcp->vc_inuse is 0 it returns -ENXIO and if the request structure cannot be allocated it returns -ENOMEM, in both cases with nothing queued and buffer still owned by the caller. Otherwise it stamps buffer->ih.unique with ++vcp->vc_seq, queues the request on vcp->vc_pending and wakes Venus. If outSize is NULL it returns 0 at once; the request now owns buffer, which the caller must not free (it is freed after Venus reads it). If outSize is non-NULL it waits (coda_waitfor_upcall): if Venus replied (CODA_REQ_WRITE) it sets *outSize to the reply size and returns -(reply result) (0 on success, the negated Venus error otherwise); if the wait ended for another reason it returns -EINTR (also when it was aborted by Venus shutdown or woke without a pending signal); when interrupted after Venus had read the request it additionally queues a CODA_SIGNAL message at the head of the pending list, but returns -ENOMEM instead of -EINTR if that signal request cannot be allocated, and queues nothing if Venus has since died. In all synchronous cases the request structure is freed here and buffer remains owned by the caller (it holds the reply when one arrived).
note: Real function, prototype-only slice. Fixed: abort/unexpected wake returns -EINTR (not -ENODEV); -ENOMEM on signal-message allocation failure.

name: coredump_parse
prose: Real function: coredump_parse(cn, cprm, argv, argc) (the packet name format_corename does not exist in this source tree, and the slice cuts the function head, so neither name is in the slice). Precondition: cn points to a writable struct core_name (its previous contents are discarded), cprm to a valid coredump_params (siginfo, mm_flags, cpu valid), argv to a size_t * and argc to an int that the caller initialised to 0 (they are used only for a '|' pipe pattern); the global core_pattern is a NUL-terminated string; the caller must kfree *argv if it was set, even when the function returns false. Postcondition: returns true only if the whole pattern was expanded. It first resets cn (mask COREDUMP_KERNEL, plus COREDUMP_WAIT when core_pipe_limit is set; used 0; core_pipe_limit 0; core_dumped false), sets core_type from the first character ('|' COREDUMP_PIPE, '@' COREDUMP_SOCK, else COREDUMP_FILE) and allocates cn->corename (false if that fails). For COREDUMP_PIPE it allocates the *argv offset array (false on allocation failure), records offset 0, skips the '|' and returns false if nothing follows. For COREDUMP_SOCK it skips '@' (a second '@' changes core_type to COREDUMP_SOCK_REQ), returns false if nothing follows or cn_printf fails, copies the rest of the pattern literally (no % expansion) and returns false unless it begins with '/', contains no space, contains no '..' path component and is shorter than UNIX_PATH_MAX; otherwise it returns true immediately. For FILE and PIPE it expands the pattern: % codes (%p %P %i %I %u %g %d %s %t %h %e %f %E %c %C %F) are expanded into cn->corename, %% gives one %, a lone trailing % is dropped, unknown codes are ignored, %F only has effect for COREDUMP_PIPE (it sets cprm->pid to the tgid and prints COREDUMP_PIDFD_NUMBER), the hostname is read under down_read(uts_sem) which is released before continuing, and for COREDUMP_PIPE spaces split the command into arguments, each start offset being appended to *argv with *argc incremented. It returns false if any cn_printf, cn_esc_printf or cn_print_exe_file call fails, and for an unknown core_type (after WARN_ON_ONCE). At the end, for COREDUMP_FILE when the pattern had no %p and core_uses_pid is set, '.<tgid>' is appended and the function returns whether that append succeeded; otherwise it returns true. No lock or reference is held on return.
note: Real function (name in packet absent from this kernel version); head cut; previous round dropped it wrongly.

name: fscrypt_decrypt_pagecache_blocks
prose: Precondition: folio points to a folio of an encrypted inode (fscrypt inode info with data unit size du_size = 1 << ci_data_unit_bits); on entry it should be locked, len is non-zero and (len | offs) is a multiple of du_size; offs + len is not checked against the folio size or for overflow. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, after a one-time warning and before touching any data, if the folio is not locked, or len is 0, or (len | offs) is not aligned to du_size. Otherwise it decrypts in place, in increasing order, each data unit of du_size bytes in the byte range [offs, offs + len) of the folio, using as data unit number (the crypto index) ((u64)folio->index << (PAGE_SHIFT - du_bits)) + (offs >> du_bits), incremented by one per unit, and returns 0; if fscrypt_crypt_data_unit fails for a unit it returns that negative errno immediately, leaving earlier units decrypted and the remaining ones untouched. The folio stays locked and no lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.
note: Fixed: index is derived from folio->index, plus offs in data units; no overflow check.

name: do_add_master_key
prose: Precondition: sb is a valid super_block, secret points to an initialised fscrypt_master_key_secret and mk_spec identifies the master key; the caller holds no fscrypt_add_key_mutex or mk->mk_sem. Postcondition: serialises with other adds via the static fscrypt_add_key_mutex (taken and released here). Looks up the key in sb->s_master_keys with fscrypt_find_master_key (taking a reference, always dropped before return). If no key struct exists it allocates the filesystem keyring if needed and calls add_new_master_key: that allocates a key struct, adds the current user to it (identifier-type keys), moves the secret into it, marks it present and inserts it in the keyring; on failure (-ENOMEM, or the error from add_master_key_user or the keyring allocation) it returns the negative error with the secret still in *secret and nothing inserted. If a key struct exists, under mk->mk_sem (write) add_existing_master_key is run: for identifier-type keys, if the current user already has a claim it returns 0 immediately without touching the secret even if the key is present; otherwise the current user is added to mk_users (an error is returned); then if the key is not present and still active the secret is moved into it and it is made present again. Thus the secret is moved out of *secret only when a new key is created or an absent key is made present again, not when the key was already present. If the old key struct turns out to have been fully removed (KEY_DEAD) it is ignored and add_new_master_key is called; if that then fails the current user may already have been added to the old struct's mk_users (not rolled back) and the secret remains in *secret. Returns 0 on success or a negative errno.
note: Corrected per round-2: success does not imply the secret was moved; user already claimed returns 0 early.

name: fscrypt_valid_enc_modes_v2
prose: Precondition: none; contents_mode and filenames_mode are arbitrary u32 encryption mode numbers (FSCRYPT_MODE_AES_256_XTS=1, AES_256_CTS=4, AES_128_CBC=5, AES_128_CTS=6, SM4_XTS=7, SM4_CTS=8, ADIANTUM=9, AES_256_HCTR2=10). Postcondition: returns true if and only if (contents_mode, filenames_mode) is one of (1, 4), (5, 6), (9, 9), (1, 10) or (7, 8), i.e. (AES_256_XTS, AES_256_CTS), (AES_128_CBC, AES_128_CTS), (ADIANTUM, ADIANTUM), (AES_256_XTS, AES_256_HCTR2) or (SM4_XTS, SM4_CTS); it returns false for every other pair. Pure: no memory, locks or references.
contract: /*@ requires 1; ensures result == ((contents_mode == 1 && filenames_mode == 4) || (contents_mode == 5 && filenames_mode == 6) || (contents_mode == 9 && filenames_mode == 9) || (contents_mode == 1 && filenames_mode == 10) || (contents_mode == 7 && filenames_mode == 8)); */
note: Constants corrected from fscrypt.h: SM4_XTS=7, SM4_CTS=8, ADIANTUM=9, AES_256_HCTR2=10.

name: d_lru_del
prose: Precondition: the caller holds dentry->d_lock; dentry is on its superblock's dentry LRU (DCACHE_LRU_LIST set) and is not on a shrink list: D_FLAG_VERIFY expects (d_flags & (DCACHE_LRU_LIST | DCACHE_SHRINK_LIST)) == DCACHE_LRU_LIST exactly and only issues a one-time warning otherwise. Postcondition: returns void. Clears DCACHE_LRU_LIST in dentry->d_flags, decrements the per-cpu nr_dentry_unused counter, additionally decrements nr_dentry_negative if the dentry is negative, and removes dentry->d_lru from dentry->d_sb->s_dentry_lru with list_lru_del_obj (a one-time WARN_ON_ONCE fires if that reports the object was not on the list). No lock or reference is acquired or released.
note: Fixed precondition: SHRINK_LIST must be clear, exact flag equality.

name: dlm_check_zero_and_dlm_running
prose: Precondition: x is any unsigned int; no locks are required and none are taken. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if x is 0 (checked first, regardless of the lowcomms state); otherwise returns -EBUSY if dlm_lowcomms_is_running() reports the lowcomms layer is running and 0 if it is not. It reads global DLM lowcomms state only and has no side effects.
note: No scalar contract: result depends on external dlm_lowcomms_is_running() state.

name: dlm_check_protocol_and_dlm_running
prose: Precondition: x is any unsigned int; no locks are required and none are taken. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if x is neither 0 (TCP) nor 1 (SCTP); returns -EOPNOTSUPP if x is 1 and the kernel was built without CONFIG_IP_SCTP; otherwise (x is 0, or x is 1 with SCTP support) returns -EBUSY if dlm_lowcomms_is_running() reports the lowcomms layer is running and 0 if it is not. It reads global DLM lowcomms state only and has no side effects.
note: No scalar contract: result depends on external lowcomms state and a build option.

name: set_lock_args
prose: Real function set_lock_args(mode, lksb, flags, namelen, ast, astparam, bast, args) (the slice cuts the head, so the name is not in the slice). Precondition: args points to writable struct dlm_args; lksb, ast and bast may be NULL pointers (ast and lksb must be non-NULL for success); no locks are required. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, leaving *args unmodified, if any of the following holds: mode is outside [0, DLM_LOCK_EX]; DLM_LKF_CONVERT is not set and namelen > DLM_RESNAME_MAXLEN; DLM_LKF_CANCEL is set; QUECVT or CONVDEADLK is set without CONVERT; CONVDEADLK together with NOQUEUE; EXPEDITE together with CONVERT, QUECVT or NOQUEUE, or with mode != DLM_LOCK_NL; ast or lksb is NULL; DLM_LKF_VALBLK is set and lksb->sb_lvbptr is NULL; DLM_LKF_CONVERT is set and lksb->sb_lkid is 0. Otherwise it sets args->flags, astfn, astparam, bastfn, mode and lksb from the parameters and returns 0. It touches no lock or reference and does not modify the lkb or lksb.
note: Slice head cut; real name set_lock_args absent from slice. Enumerated every -EINVAL condition.

name: validate_unlock_args
prose: Precondition: lkb and args are valid, lkb->lkb_resource->res_ls is a valid lockspace, and the caller holds the lock required to inspect the lkb (the rsb lock) as usual for unlock/cancel. Postcondition: returns 0 only through the out_ok path, after OR-ing args->flags into lkb->lkb_exflags, setting the lkb's sbflags to 0 and lkb->lkb_astparam = args->astparam. Returns -EBUSY (with the lkb otherwise unchanged except as noted) if: a normal unlock (neither CANCEL nor FORCEUNLOCK) finds lkb_wait_type or lkb_wait_count non-zero; the lkb is on a pending rsb lookup list (when CANCEL or FORCEUNLOCK is set it is additionally removed from the lookup list, a cast of -DLM_ECANCEL or -DLM_EUNLOCK is queued and the lookup's lkb reference is dropped with unhold_lkb, and the caller converts that -EBUSY to 0); a CANCEL or FORCEUNLOCK finds the RESEND flag set (setting DLM_IFL_OVERLAP_CANCEL or OVERLAP_UNLOCK respectively); a CANCEL finds a granted lkb with no wait in progress (nothing to cancel); or a CANCEL/FORCEUNLOCK finds a LOOKUP or REQUEST in the wait state (setting the overlap CANCEL/UNLOCK bit). Returns -EINVAL (with WARN_ON and an error log, lkb unchanged) for a master copy (DLM_IFL_MSTCPY), when is_overlap_unlock(lkb), when CANCEL is requested and lkb_exflags already has CANCEL or is_overlap_cancel(lkb) holds or the wait type is UNLOCK or CANCEL, and when FORCEUNLOCK is requested and lkb_exflags already has FORCEUNLOCK or the wait type is UNLOCK. Returns -ENOENT (debug log only) for an end-of-life lkb. On a normal unlock or cancel that passes all checks no wait bit is set here (add_to_waiters sets the overlap bits later).
note: Fixed per round-2: CANCEL/UNLOCK-in-progress and overlap-cancel cases return -EINVAL; added is_overlap_unlock -EINVAL.
